entity_relationships.base: perform contract or customer-directed work on
entity_relationships.third_person: performs contract or customer-directed work on
entity_relationships.gerund: performing contract or customer-directed work on

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: At least one {{entity_noun}} is explicitly stated in the phrase or its relationship summary.

children.text: It must be stated, not inferred. It may not be derived from industry context, markets served, certifications, standards, equipment, facilities, materials, or process names. A named process or capability with no stated output does not satisfy this condition. A phrase naming a specific item does satisfy it — name the category that item belongs to, never its brand, model, or part number.

rules.text: The phrase and its relationship summary show real, concrete involvement with the identified {{entity_noun}}: some party is shown to {{entity_relationships.base}} that {{entity_noun}}, not merely to name, list, or mention it in passing.

children.text: The work must be placed on the other party's side of the arrangement: items in the {{entity_noun}} belong to, are specified by, or are branded for a customer, client, OEM, or brand owner — produced, machined, assembled, formulated, finished, packaged, or otherwise made to their specification, design, drawing, formula, or brand.
Selling them is NOT required. In contract work the customer owns and sells them, so the absence of any sale by the manufacturer is not a reason to fail.

rules.text: It is the manufacturer itself that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} the identified {{entity_noun}} — not a customer, supplier, distributor, or other third party that the manufacturer merely relates to.

children.text: Verbs that leave the arrangement unstated — such as "supplies", "offers", "provides", "works with", "handles", or "deals in" — do not by themselves show whether the manufacturer is the party that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} it.
The manufacturer must be the shop doing the work, not the party sending it out. A phrase showing that someone else performs the contract work on items in the {{entity_noun}} fails this condition.

Judge each candidate on its own. A phrase that also describes products the manufacturer makes and sells as its own still passes on a different candidate that clears this condition, so rule the failing candidate out and go on to the next one rather than rejecting the phrase. A phrase may legitimately pass both this screen and the separate own-product screen.

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} is ruled out if ANY of these guards is violated by it. Ruling out one candidate does not reject the phrase — another candidate may still qualify:

rules.text: The manufacturer's contract or customer-directed work on the identified {{entity_noun}} is only aspirational, hoped-for, planned, or discontinued, rather than current and actual.
